title: Beau Lamarre-Condon trial: crime scene photos paint harrowing picture of alleged murder victims’ final moments
summary:
Former police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in early 2024

Warning: graphic content

blocks.text: Warning: graphic content
A hole in a door and a bullet bent out of shape: crime scene photos shown to a jury paint a harrowing picture of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies’ final moments.
Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting the couple with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
Photos from Baird’s eastern suburbs terrace house were revealed to the court during his trial on Tuesday before later being released to the media.
In some images, Baird’s bedroom, back courtyard and a bathroom glow with luminol after the chemical, which highlights possible blood staining, was used by police to examine the home.

blocks.caption: Exhibit from the trial of  Beau Lamarre-Condon showing Jesse Baird’s back courtyard during luminol analysis. The chemical highlights possible bloodstaining. Photograph: Supreme Court of NSW

blocks.text: An image taken in the sub-floor beneath Baird’s ground floor bedroom – accessed by a trap-door in the room – shows a bloodstained tarpaulin.
Referring to a photo of a misshapen and bloodstained bullet, Bronwyn Lansley, a crime scene officer, explained it had travelled through a source of blood before penetrating the wooden flooring.
A bullet hole in the door of Baird’s bedroom was also shown to the court.
Investigators explained it had not been discovered until July, two months before the trial, as it had been repaired with putty and covered with a mounting hook.
Analysis of stippling marks left on the door when the gun was fired showed there was nothing between the muzzle of the firearm and the door, Lansley said.

The prosecution alleges Lamarre-Condon began cleaning up the crime scene immediately after the shootings, before dumping Baird and Davies’ bloodied belongings in a skip bin at the Cronulla Bowls Club.
More than 100 photos of the bin’s contents were shown on Wednesday.
Many of the items were covered in blood, including a white t-shirt, jewellery, and a bed sheet.

Baird had been a TV presenter and AFL goal umpire, while Davies was a flight attendant.
Among the items were bloodstained AFL goal umpire flags, caps and shorts still in their plastic packaging, and a wallet containing Davies’ Qantas ID card.

Crime scene officer Sen Sgt Bronwyn Lansley confirmed to the court that a bloodied shoe print found on the hem of a hoodie pulled from the dumpster matched prints discovered near a monastery in Bungonia, where Baird and Davies’ bodies were eventually discovered.

blocks.caption: Exhibit from the trail of  Beau Lamarre-Condon showing a bathroom in Jesse Baird’s Paddington home, with alleged blood stains glowing with luminol. Photograph: Supreme Court of NSW

blocks.text: Defence lawyer John Stratton SC said during his opening statement that Baird and Davies were fatally shot in “self-defence” following struggles with the policeman.
Lamarre-Condon immediately began cleaning up the scene because he “panicked”, the jury was told.
The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.
